commits.edited_message:
reject oversized and truncated Huffman-table streams

Each Huffman group has 5 trees, each requiring at least 4 bits in the bitstream (20 bits per group). Verify that the remaining unread bits in dec->br can cover num_htree_groups_max before allocating code_lengths, htree_groups, and huffman_tables.

Also reject group counts whose worst-case table allocation exceeds the existing MAX_HUFF_IMAGE_SIZE ceiling before allocating.

BUG: 550179426

Change-Id: I87d884bd216f47789b76ac875018a19fc674dd4f

allocate HTreeGroup::packed_table from HuffmanTables

Replace the inline 512-byte packed_table[HUFFMAN_PACKED_TABLE_SIZE] array in HTreeGroup with a HuffmanCode32* pointer carved out of the global HuffmanTables segment linked list, reducing sizeof(HTreeGroup) without per-group allocations.

Bound each segment chunk by the color-cache-aware number of groups it can contain. Also support 12-bit color caches; the precomputed table sizes continue to cover the original range, and larger cache sizes use a conservative computed bound.

Change-Id: Ia7ec942b7d003119f00f1289de940e0d248cd5f2

coupling: The first edited commit adds a pre-allocation ceiling check that directly indexes kTableSize[color_cache_bits]. That lookup is in-bounds in its own tree because MAX_CACHE_BITS is still 11 and kTableSize has entries for cache bits 0 through 11. The later edited commit raises MAX_CACHE_BITS to 12 and moves its own primary table sizing to GetHuffmanTableSize(), which safely handles the new range, but it does not reconcile the earlier commit's direct lookup. Only their composition accepts a VP8L stream with 12 color-cache bits and then reaches kTableSize[12], reading one element past the global table. The first commit alone still rejects 12-bit caches; the later commit alone routes its own sizing through the safe helper. A maintenance-preserving fix must make the earlier preflight consumer use the same 12-bit-aware sizing as the later allocator (or extend the shared table), so it has to reason across both commits.
